IgM-enriched immunoglobulins (IVIG) are being explored as an adjuvant therapy in septic very low birth weight (VLBW) infants. Studies have shown that IVIG can be effective in reducing morbidity and mortality associated with sepsis, particularly in this vulnerable population.

In a hypothesis-generator study, the researchers found that IgM-enriched immunoglobulins were an effective adjuvant therapy in VLBW infants with proven sepsis. However, it is essential to note that these findings are based on pilot observations and require further confirmation through randomized controlled trials.

To summarize, IgM-enriched immunoglobulins may be a promising treatment option for septic VLBW infants, but more research is needed to confirm its effectiveness and optimal dosing strategy.
